raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Kimi-K3's token-major prefill convolution leaves strided Q/K/V views, and its merged gate projection leaves a strided beta view. FlashInfer's KDA wrapper materializes these inputs with separate copies. Batch those required copies into one Triton launch without changing KDA arithmetic, gates, state precision, or checkpoint handling.

This integrates the measured PP8 prototype into upstream `main`. Full-model serving validation now passes for these production changes on the common upstream `main` base `592754fc5e`, with FlashInfer 0.7.2; the standalone and repeated combined results are reported below. Real GPU operator tests pass on both FlashInfer 0.7.1 and the pinned 0.7.2.

### Relationship to sgl-project/sglang#47451

The optimizations overlap on the Q/K/V materialization cost, but use different approaches:

- #47451 changes the convolution producer to write contiguous Q/K/V groups, eliminating those three copies. It also covers the FlashInfer prefill-graph producer path.
- This PR leaves the producer layout alone and combines outstanding consumer-side copies, including beta. It covers both `FlashInferKDAPrefillKernel.extend` and `FlashInferKDAPrefillGraph.run` through the same helper.
- Contiguous inputs are returned unchanged. When fewer than two inputs require copying (e.g. grouped Q/K/V plus only strided beta), the ordinary contiguous path is retained. There is no redundant Q/K/V copy or extra fused-copy launch in that case.
- Their standalone speedups must **not** be added. Prefer the producer-layout solution where applicable; this is a separately reviewable alternative for remaining token-major inputs, not a second claimed gain on top of #47451.

## Modifications

- Add a bit-preserving multi-input copy kernel under `kernels/ops/attention` and use it at the FlashInfer KDA input boundary.
- Keep contiguous tensors aliased, validate device/dtype/indexing bounds, and fall back to PyTorch for unsupported inputs or autograd.
- Preserve input slicing and all existing KDA computation arguments. No new environment variable or CLI option.
- Add registered GPU coverage for the real 16K/96-head K3 layout, short/tail/empty shapes, BF16/FP32 bit patterns, already-grouped QKV, CUDA Graph replay, and real FlashInfer outputs/state.

## Accuracy Tests

On an idle B300/B30Z (SM103), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, separately using FlashInfer 0.7.1 and 0.7.2:

- **5 GPU tests passed on each version**, including actual Triton execution at `[1, 16384, 96, 128]` and CUDA Graph replay with changed inputs.
- Raw-bit comparisons cover NaN payloads, infinities, subnormals, and signed zero.
- Real FlashInfer KDA calls on strided inputs match contiguous-reference outputs and recurrent state exactly, in eager mode and through the production graph adapter replayed with updated inputs. Warmup and capture use the same stream, as required by the FlashInfer workspace.
- The candidate kernel and wrapper were loaded from this branch into the existing GPU environment; no installed source was modified. FlashInfer 0.7.2 was tested in an isolated wheel overlay without bypassing its version checks.
- Ruff, isort, AST parsing, registered-test lint, and `git diff --check` passed.

The current six full-service runs each pass 12 fixed greedy output checks covering input lengths 1,024 / 16,383 / 16,384 / 16,385 / 32,768 / 65,536, each repeated twice. All 60 comparisons against A1 match output token IDs and input SHA256 hashes. An additional eight C4 concurrent fixed-input checks match between A2 and B2. These are finite output-regression checks, not logits-level equality or a full task-accuracy benchmark.

### Blackwell review follow-up (2026-11-01)

Reran both complete files on B300/B30Z (SM103), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 and FlashInfer 0.7.2, using the complete Python tree from PR head `7933473906e291d9a14d26ba78aca0284820ae1e`:

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_kda_input_pack.py`: **5 tests passed, 0 skipped**.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_kda_prefill_graph.py`: **9 tests passed, 0 skipped**, including the FlashInfer/Blackwell cases that were skipped on the H100 CI runner.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Full serving validation of the upstream integration (2026-11-01)

Tested production changes from #47651 (`7933473906e`) and #47653 (`34238f31a5d`) on the same upstream `main` base `592754fc5e`, using FlashInfer 0.7.2 for every arm. Kimi-K3, one 8-GPU B300/B30Z, TP1/PP8/EP1, chunk 16,384, pipeline async depth 1, client C4, ISL 65,536 / OSL 1. CUDA Graphs and radix caching disabled; model precision and all serving settings held fixed. Each formal run contains 128 requests after a separate 8-request warmup. Formal measurements exclude profiler/diagnostic requests and prototype hooks.

Each run uses an independent autotune cache cloned from the same baseline startup cache. Baseline/KDA caches contain no 16K MoE seed; MoE/combined caches contain the FlashInfer 0.7.2 `(128, 4)` record on all eight PP ranks. Separate post-benchmark Torch GPU traces of all eight PP ranks confirm the actual production paths: 1,104 KDA input-copy kernels become 276 pack kernels, and all 736 MoE GEMMs change token tile 192 to 128. These C1 diagnostic traces verify execution paths; their timings are not used as C4 serving measurements.

| Run | Requests | Input tok/s | P50 TTFT s | P99 TTFT s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline A1 | 128 | 42,203.78 | 6.128 | 7.046 |
| KDA only | 128 | 42,899.91 | 6.022 | 6.937 |
| MoE only | 128 | 42,813.05 | 6.034 | 6.926 |
| combined B1 | 128 | 43,569.94 | 5.925 | 6.835 |
| baseline A2 | 128 | 42,130.58 | 6.137 | 7.050 |
| combined B2 | 128 | 43,524.13 | 5.940 | 6.823 |
| baseline pooled | 256 | 42,167.15 | 6.132 | 7.359 |
| combined pooled | 256 | 43,547.02 | 5.930 | 7.125 |

KDA-only throughput changes by +1.65% against A1. This is one standalone screening pair. The repeated combined KDA+MoE result changes throughput by +3.27% (paired runs +3.24% / +3.31%); it must not be attributed to either PR alone. Pooled throughput is total input tokens / total formal duration; P50/P99 are recomputed from all formal request TTFTs. All 768 formal requests succeed with zero cached tokens and retractions. The combined pooled P50/P99 TTFT decrease by 3.28% / 3.17%; no formal request reaches 15 seconds. OSL is 1, so TPOT/ITL are not reported.

### Earlier prototype evidence

**Historical prototype results, not a new end-to-end benchmark of this branch.** Kimi-K3 / SGLang 0.5.22 / FlashInfer 0.7.1, one 8-GPU B300, TP1/PP8, chunk 16,384, client concurrency 4, ISL 65,536 / OSL 1. CUDA Graphs and radix caching disabled; all model precision settings unchanged. Warmups and profiling requests excluded.

| Run | Requests | Input tok/s | P50 TTFT s | P99 TTFT s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline A1 | 128 | 41,924.66 | 6.161 | 7.135 |
| pack B1 | 128 | 42,610.43 | 6.062 | 7.022 |
| baseline A2 | 128 | 41,811.10 | 6.176 | 7.110 |
| pack B2 | 128 | 42,526.45 | 6.078 | 6.996 |
| baseline pooled | 256 | 41,867.80 | 6.164 | 7.438 |
| pack pooled | 256 | 42,568.40 | 6.071 | 7.320 |

Pooled throughput changes by **+1.67%**. Throughput uses total tokens / total duration; percentiles are recomputed from all formal requests, not averaged between runs. All requests succeeded with no cache hits or retractions. Only one output token is generated, so TPOT/ITL are not reported.

The combined prototype's NSYS trace showed KDA copy-related time changing from 1.5405 to 0.3566 ms per matched layer invocation. That includes remaining copies and is not the complete KDA layer time. Required element traffic is unchanged. The combined MoE+KDA serving gain is not attributed to this PR alone.

## Checklist

- [x] Keep arithmetic and precision unchanged; add no configuration switch.
- [x] Run actual GPU copy, graph replay, and FlashInfer output/state checks.
- [x] Document overlap with #47451 and avoid redundant work with grouped QKV.
- [x] Separate prototype performance evidence from exact-branch validation.
- [x] Complete common-base full-model serving validation, including repeated baseline/combined A/B and fixed output checks.

detail.title: [Perf] kda: Batch strided FlashInfer prefill input copies

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,100 @@
+"""Materialize FlashInfer KDA's strided inputs in one copy launch."""
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _copy_strided(
+    X,
+    Y,
+    block_id,
+    SHAPE: tl.constexpr,
+    STRIDES: tl.constexpr,
+    SIZE: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    linear = block_id * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    remaining = linear
+    source = tl.full((BLOCK,), 0, tl.int32)
+    for dim in tl.static_range(len(SHAPE) - 1, -1, -1):
+        source += (remaining % SHAPE[dim]) * STRIDES[dim]
+        remaining //= SHAPE[dim]
+    # Copy the representation, including BF16 NaN payloads and signed zero.
+    if X.dtype.element_ty == tl.bfloat16:
+        X = X.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.uint16))
+        Y = Y.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.uint16))
+    else:
+        X = X.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.uint32))
+        Y = Y.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.uint32))
+    value = tl.load(X + source, linear < SIZE, other=0)
+    tl.store(Y + linear, value, linear < SIZE)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _pack_kda_inputs(
+    sources,
+    destinations,
+    SHAPES: tl.constexpr,
+    STRIDES: tl.constexpr,
+    SIZES: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    block_id = tl.program_id(0)
+    start = 0
+    for i in tl.static_range(len(SIZES)):
+        if SIZES[i] > 0:
+            blocks = tl.cdiv(SIZES[i], BLOCK)
+            if (block_id >= start) & (block_id < start + blocks):
+                _copy_strided(
+                    sources[i],
+                    destinations[i],
+                    block_id - start,
+                    SHAPES[i],
+                    STRIDES[i],
+                    SIZES[i],
+                    BLOCK,
+                )
+            start += blocks
+
+
+def contiguous_kda_inputs(q, k, v, g, beta):
+    """Preserve each input's values, dtype, shape, and the current CUDA stream.
+
+    Convolution outputs that already provide contiguous Q/K/V groups need at
+    most the beta copy. Keep those on the ordinary path; this kernel targets
+    the multiple strided views produced by token-major QKV convolution.
+    """
+    tensors = (q, k, v, g, beta)
+    sizes = tuple(0 if t.is_contiguous() else t.numel() for t in tensors)
+    if not any(sizes):
+        return tensors
+    if sum(n > 0 for n in sizes) < 2 or not all(
+        t.is_cuda
+        and t.device == q.device
+        and t.dtype in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float32)
+        and not t.requires_grad
+        and 1 <= t.ndim <= 4
+        and t.numel() < 2**31
+        and all(s >= 0 for s in t.stride())
+        and sum((d - 1) * s for d, s in zip(t.shape, t.stride())) < 2**31
+        for t in tensors
+    ):
+        return tuple(t.contiguous() for t in tensors)
+    outputs = tuple(
+        torch.empty(t.shape, dtype=t.dtype, device=t.device) if n else t
+        for t, n in zip(tensors, sizes)
+    )
+    block = 4096
+    with torch.cuda.device(q.device):
+        _pack_kda_inputs[(sum(triton.cdiv(n, block) for n in sizes),)](
+            tensors,
+            outputs,
+            tuple(tuple(t.shape) for t in tensors),
+            tuple(tuple(t.stride()) for t in tensors),
+            sizes,
+            block,
+            num_warps=8,
+        )
+    return outputs

 import torch
 import torch.nn.functional as F
 
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.kda_input_pack import contiguous_kda_inputs
+
 
 class FlashInferKDAPrefillGraph:

                 checkpoint_every_n_tokens=64,
             )
+        q, k, v, g, beta = contiguous_kda_inputs(q, k, v, g, beta)
         return wrapper.run(
-            q=q.contiguous(),
-            k=k.contiguous(),
-            v=v.contiguous(),
-            g=g.contiguous(),
-            beta=beta.contiguous(),
+            q=q,
+            k=k,
+            v=v,
+            g=g,
+            beta=beta,
             A_log=layer.A_log.reshape(-1).float().contiguous(),

             initial_state=ssm_states,

@@ -7,6 +7,7 @@

+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.kda_input_pack import contiguous_kda_inputs
 from sglang.srt.layers.attention.linear.kernels.kernel_backend import (
     LinearAttnKernelBase,
 )
@@ -118,12 +119,15 @@ def extend(
             if needs_checkpoint

+        q, k, v, g, beta = contiguous_kda_inputs(
+            q, k, v, g[:, : q.shape[1]], beta[:, : q.shape[1]]
+        )
         result = self._recurrent_kda(
-            q=q.contiguous(),
-            k=k.contiguous(),
-            v=v.contiguous(),
-            g=g[:, : q.shape[1]].contiguous(),
-            beta=beta[:, : q.shape[1]].contiguous(),
+            q=q,
+            k=k,
+            v=v,
+            g=g,
+            beta=beta,
             A_log=A_log.reshape(-1).float().contiguous(),
             # FlashInfer's grouped-CTA recurrent kernel (extends with a cached prefix)
             # indexes dt_bias as a flat [H*K] tensor and asserts a unit leading stride.

@@ -0,0 +1,171 @@
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.kda_input_pack import contiguous_kda_inputs
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=10, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+
+def make_inputs(tokens, heads=96, dim=128, dtype=torch.bfloat16):
+    # The real K3 convolution and merged f_a/beta projection layouts.
+    qkv = torch.empty(tokens, 3 * heads * dim, dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
+    qkv.view(torch.uint8).random_(0, 256)
+    q, k, v = (x.reshape(1, tokens, heads, dim) for x in qkv.chunk(3, -1))
+    g = torch.zeros_like(q, memory_format=torch.contiguous_format)
+    bfa = torch.empty(tokens, 128 + heads, dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
+    bfa.view(torch.uint8).random_(0, 256)
+    beta = bfa[:, 128:].unsqueeze(0)
+    return q, k, v, g, beta
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(torch.cuda.is_available(), "requires CUDA")
+class TestKDAInputPack(CustomTestCase):
+    def assert_packed(self, inputs, outputs):
+        for source, output in zip(inputs, outputs):
+            self.assertTrue(output.is_contiguous())
+            self.assertEqual(source.dtype, output.dtype)
+            self.assertTrue(
+                torch.equal(
+                    source.contiguous().view(torch.uint8), output.view(torch.uint8)
+                )
+            )
+            if source.is_contiguous():
+                self.assertEqual(source.data_ptr(), output.data_ptr())
+
+    def test_real_layout_bits_and_tails(self):
+        # Random raw bits cover NaNs, infinities, subnormals and signed zero.
+        for tokens, heads, dim, dtype in (
+            (16384, 96, 128, torch.bfloat16),
+            (257, 6, 128, torch.bfloat16),
+            (17, 3, 65, torch.float32),
+            (0, 3, 65, torch.bfloat16),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(tokens=tokens, dtype=dtype):
+                inputs = make_inputs(tokens, heads, dim, dtype)
+                self.assert_packed(inputs, contiguous_kda_inputs(*inputs))
+
+    def test_grouped_qkv_and_contiguous_inputs(self):
+        inputs = make_inputs(257, 6)
+        grouped = tuple(t.contiguous() for t in inputs[:4]) + inputs[4:]
+        self.assert_packed(grouped, contiguous_kda_inputs(*grouped))
+        dense = tuple(t.contiguous() for t in inputs)
+        outputs = contiguous_kda_inputs(*dense)
+        self.assertTrue(all(a is b for a, b in zip(dense, outputs)))
+
+    def test_cuda_graph_replays_current_values(self):
+        inputs = make_inputs(257, 6)
+        stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+        stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+        with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+            for _ in range(3):
+                contiguous_kda_inputs(*inputs)
+        torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            outputs = contiguous_kda_inputs(*inputs)
+        for value in (0.0, -0.0, float("inf"), float("nan")):
+            for t in inputs:
+                t.fill_(value)
+            graph.replay()
+            self.assert_packed(inputs, outputs)
+
+    def test_flashinfer_output_and_state(self):
+        if torch.cuda.get_device_capability() not in ((10, 0), (10, 3)):
+            self.skipTest("FlashInfer KDA requires Blackwell")
+        from sglang.srt.layers.attention.linear.kernels.kda_flashinfer_prefill import (
+            FlashInferKDAPrefillKernel,
+        )
+
+        inputs = make_inputs(257, 6)
+        for t in inputs:
+            t.normal_(0, 0.1)
+        dense = tuple(t.contiguous() for t in inputs)
+        kernel = FlashInferKDAPrefillKernel()
+        states = torch.zeros(2, 6, 128, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        kwargs = dict(
+            cache_indices=torch.tensor([1], device="cuda"),
+            query_start_loc=torch.tensor([0, 257], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+            A_log=torch.zeros(6, device="cuda"),
+            dt_bias=torch.zeros(768, device="cuda"),
+            lower_bound=-5.0,
+        )
+        expected_states = states.clone()
+        expected = kernel.extend(*dense, ssm_states=expected_states, **kwargs)
+        actual = kernel.extend(*inputs, ssm_states=states, **kwargs)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(expected, actual))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(expected_states, states))
+
+    def test_flashinfer_graph_adapter_replay(self):
+        if torch.cuda.get_device_capability() not in ((10, 0), (10, 3)):
+            self.skipTest("FlashInfer KDA requires Blackwell")
+        from sglang.srt.layers.attention.linear.kda_flashinfer_prefill_graph import (
+            FlashInferKDAPrefillGraph,
+        )
+        from sglang.srt.layers.attention.linear.kernels.kda_flashinfer_prefill import (
+            FlashInferKDAPrefillKernel,
+        )
+
+        kernel = FlashInferKDAPrefillKernel()
+        if kernel.prefill_graph_wrapper_cls is None:
+            self.skipTest("FlashInfer does not provide the prefill graph wrapper")
+        inputs = make_inputs(257, 6)
+        for t in inputs:
+            t.normal_(0, 0.1)
+        states = torch.zeros(2, 6, 128, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        layer = SimpleNamespace(
+            layer_id=0,
+            A_log=torch.zeros(6, device="cuda"),
+            dt_bias=torch.zeros(768, device="cuda"),
+            lower_bound=-5.0,
+        )
+        adapter = FlashInferKDAPrefillGraph(
+            wrapper_cls=kernel.prefill_graph_wrapper_cls,
+            num_tokens=257,
+            max_seqs=1,
+            track=False,
+            device="cuda",
+        )
+        adapter.cu_seqlens.copy_(torch.tensor([0, 257], device="cuda"))
+        adapter.cache_indices.fill_(1)
+
+        def run():
+            return adapter.run(
+                layer=layer,
+                **dict(zip(("q", "k", "v", "g", "beta"), inputs)),
+                ssm_states=states,
+                h_track=None,
+            )
+
+        stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+        stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+        with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+            run()
+        torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
+            actual = run()
+        for _ in range(2):
+            for t in inputs:
+                t.normal_(0, 0.1)
+            states.zero_()
+            expected_states = states.clone()
+            expected = kernel.extend(
+                *(t.contiguous() for t in inputs),
+                ssm_states=expected_states,
+                cache_indices=adapter.cache_indices,
+                query_start_loc=adapter.cu_seqlens,
+                A_log=layer.A_log,
+                dt_bias=layer.dt_bias,
+                lower_bound=layer.lower_bound,
+            )
+            graph.replay()
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(expected, actual))
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(expected_states, states))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
